answer.decision: Choose continuous transaction-log backups with weekly full database backups, lifecycle-tier older backups, retain 12 months of month-end recoverability, and test restores regularly.
answer.action: Set the transaction-log backup interval to no more than 15 minutes; retain complete full-and-log recovery chains for each required month-end point; keep recent recovery data in fast storage and tier older eligible chains to cold storage; run restore drills that include cold retrieval and all operational steps; and validate projected savings before rollout, proceeding only if the model confirms at least a 35% monthly cost reduction.
reasons: Log backups at intervals of 15 minutes or less can satisfy the database RPO, provided the recovery chain remains complete.
A weekly-full-plus-logs restore completed in 76 minutes; adding the maximum 20-minute cold-retrieval delay yields 96 minutes, leaving 24 minutes within the 2-hour RTO.
Daily full database backups account for 72% of current backup storage cost, so replacing most daily fulls addresses the dominant cost driver.
Compliance requires 12 months of month-end recoverability, not one year of daily full images.
Cold storage costs 68% less per GB, making lifecycle tiering a strong additional savings lever.
Keeping daily fulls relies on uncertain negotiated pricing, while reducing all retention to 30 days would violate the compliance requirement.
assumptions: Transaction logs can be captured, replicated, monitored, and retained at intervals no longer than 15 minutes without gaps.
The 76-minute restore drill is representative of production recovery and includes all material restoration work other than any cold-tier retrieval delay.
Cold retrieval adds no more than 20 minutes and required objects can be retrieved without significant serial delays.
Retention rules can preserve every full backup and log segment needed to reconstruct each required month-end state.
A detailed cost model will confirm the mandatory 35% reduction before implementation.
risks: The supplied evidence does not by itself prove that the proposed policy will reduce total monthly backup cost by at least 35%.
Missing or corrupt log segments could break point-in-time or month-end recovery chains.
Production growth, decryption, contention, validation, or operational handoffs could exceed the 24-minute modeled RTO margin for cold-tier restores.
Incorrect lifecycle or expiration rules could delete dependencies needed for retained recovery points.
Log storage accumulates at an average of 6% of a daily full per day and must be included in retention and cost calculations.

citations.claim: Database RPO is at most 15 minutes, database RTO is at most 2 hours, and monthly backup storage cost must fall by at least 35%.
Daily full database backups account for 72% of current backup storage cost.
Point-in-time recovery logs average 6% of a daily full backup's storage per day.
Compliance requires 12 months of month-end recoverability rather than daily full images.
A weekly-full-plus-logs restore completed in 76 minutes.
Cold-tier storage costs 68% less per GB and can add up to 20 minutes of retrieval delay.
Document objects already use lifecycle tiering, making database backups the dominant remaining cost lever.
